content_html:
If you're planning an epic hike to Machu Picchu, you're probably wondering which is the best option: the traditional Inca Trail or the challenging Salkantay Route. Both offer unforgettable experiences, but they have key differences that can help you make the best decision based on your style of adventure.

Inca Trail: The Classic Route

Main Features:

  • Distance: Approximately 42 km
  • Duration: 4 days / 3 nights
  • Maximum Altitude: 4,215 m (Warmiwañusca Pass)
  • Difficulty: Moderate to challenging
  • Landscapes: Inca ruins, cloud forests and mountains
  • Access to Machu Picchu: Entrance through Puerta del Sol

Advantages:

Historical and heritage route

Exclusive walk with limited spaces

Direct access to Machu Picchu

Disadvantages:

Reservation required months in advance

Strict regulations

Salkantay: The Scenic Alternative

Main Features:

  • Distance: Approximately 72 km
  • Duration: 5 days / 4 nights
  • Maximum Altitude: 4,650 m (Salkantay Pass)
  • Difficulty: Challenging
  • Landscapes: Snowy mountains, lagoons and jungle
  • Access to Machu Picchu: From Aguas Calientes

Advantages:

More availability and flexibility

Stunning natural landscapes

Does not require special permissions

Disadvantages:

Greater distance and physical effort

Does not include direct entry to Machu Picchu

Which one to choose?

  • If you are interested in history and an exclusive route: Inca Trail
  • If you prefer impressive landscapes and more freedom: Salkantay

Both options guarantee an incredible experience, it just depends on your preference and level of adventure. Which one do you choose for your next expedition?
